messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batching runtime cluster 'us-west-2-rb-3' p95 latency spike > 2s, error rate increased (5xxs). auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

alex: paging in. seeing queue depth climb on runtime pods, microbatch sizes jumping to 64-128 despite config target 8.

priya: confirmed - kv-cache memory for shard-7 shot to 92% and eviction thrash started. looks like client-side prefix growth + missing cache aging.

ben: are customers impacted? any big users in the affected shard?

sara: yes — two active Dedicated customers on that shard reporting timeouts (~30s) and partial responses. prod_support notified them (initial msg).

prod_support: notified customer A and B, they're seeing partial generations and retries. asked for ETA and mitigation.

alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce MAX_MICROBATCH to 8 on affected routers 2) temporarily disable continuous batching for shard-7 3) evict oldest KV cache prefixes to free memory.

priya: agree. pushing small hotfix flag change now via control plane. command: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags -d '{"shard":"shard-7","CONT_BATCH_ENABLED":false,"MAX_MICROBATCH":8}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN'`

ben: i'm running kv evict script against shard-7: `./kv-cache-ctl evict --shard shard-7 --policy lru --bytes 2G`

sara: i'm coordinating restarts: we should do rolling restart on runtime pods after flags applied to avoid cold-start KV regen. doing 1 pod at a time.

incident-bot: ACTION: flag change accepted, rolling flag rollout started (3/3 nodes updated).

alex: flags are live. starting rolling restarts now. watch metrics.

priya: after first pod restart, p95 dropped from 2100ms -> 720ms, error rate edged down. queue depth also reduced.

ben: kv eviction completed, freed ~1.9GB on shard-7, swap pressure relieved.

sara: second pod restart done. no new 5xxs. customers report partial recovery. prod_support updated.

prod_support: customers A/B confirmed retries now succeed, latency improved. still see occasional timeouts on very long contexts.

alex: keep continuous batching disabled until we have a safe jitter/microbatch guard. priya, can you add a guard in the router to cap microbatch size and add randomized jitter to batch start?

priya: yes - I'll push a patch to runtime: add per-tenant batch cap and jitter window (configurable). PR created: runtime#4527. will QA on staging.

ben: adding monitoring alerts for sudden kv-cache growth and microbatch-burst > 2x expected. alert rule drafted.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: impact reduced, mitigation applied (flags + eviction + restarts). severity -> P2 pending postmortem.

alex: handing off to ben for overnight monitoring. I'm logging incident timeline and initial notes in the incident doc. ben, take pager for next 6h?

ben: taking handoff. I'll keep watch and escalate if any reappearance. linking grafana dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/abc/continuous-batch-overview

sara: I'll coordinate post-incident customer follow-ups with prod_support tomorrow AM.

prod_support: will send formal update to affected customers summarizing mitigation and next steps.

priya: follow-ups: 1) implement batch cap + jitter PR 2) add kv-cache aging/backpressure 3) run load testing at high concurrency to reproduce microbatch blowups.

alex: agree. I'll schedule a blameless postmortem. assigning owners: priya -> patch + tests, ben -> alerts + runbook, sara -> customer comms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated): 2026-06-14T02:30:01Z.

ben: quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely interplay of rapid concurrent requests + missing per-tenant microbatch cap causing batching to coalesce into very large microbatches, which in turn caused KV cache working set to spike and thrash evictions, leading to increased latency and 5xxs.

sara: thanks team. I'll drop the initial customer communication in #marketing-customer-comm later today.

alex: good job everyone. we'll track follow-ups in the incident doc and close when PRs are merged and tests pass. :thumbsup:
